decisions.bounded_context_strategy: By epic - Each epic represents a bounded context
decisions.concept_discovery_source: Story map + existing docs - Include concepts from current documentation
decisions.domain_detail_level: Moderate - Concept names, responsibilities, key relationships
decisions.domain_modeling_approach: Hybrid - Mix of approaches based on subdomain complexity
decisions.relationship_depth: Basic relationships - Collaborators with relationship types (has-a, uses, contains)

rationale.bounded_context_strategy: The four epics represent distinct bounded contexts: 1) Foundry API Integration - system interaction concerns, 2) Mob Management - mob lifecycle and CRUD operations, 3) Strategy Management - targeting and behavior rules, 4) Combat Execution - action coordination and execution. Each has cohesive domain concepts with clear boundaries.
rationale.concept_discovery_source: We have the story map from shaping phase and the original input.txt describing the system vision and high-level concepts (mob, minions, strategies, Foundry VTT). These together provide comprehensive concept sources without needing interviews or code.
rationale.domain_detail_level: This is a focused enhancement to Foundry VTT, not a complex enterprise domain. Moderate detail (names, responsibilities, key relationships) provides sufficient clarity without over-engineering. We can add more detail during design/implementation if needed.
rationale.domain_modeling_approach: Hybrid approach fits best: DDD for core concepts (Mob as aggregate root, Minion, Strategy as value objects), Event-Driven for combat flows (Target Selected, Attack Executed), Resource-Oriented for Foundry integration (Token, Actor, Combat Tracker). Each subdomain has different complexity requiring different modeling styles.
rationale.relationship_depth: Basic relationships (has-a, uses, contains) are sufficient to show how concepts collaborate. We don't need full cardinality and lifecycle dependencies for this focused enhancement. Relationship types will clarify structural (has-a, contains) vs behavioral (uses, interacts-with) connections.

accepted: Domain concepts emerge from stories and business language, not technical implementation
Use ubiquitous language from domain experts (GM, mob, minion, strategy, swarm, token, actor)
Model domain concepts, not technical classes or database tables
Focus on core domain concepts first (Mob, Minion, Strategy, Target) then supporting concepts
Concepts placed at most specific level (sub-epic) and elevated only if shared across contexts
Each bounded context has its own view - e.g., 'Target' means different things in Targeting vs Combat contexts
Domain concepts capture WHAT exists (Mob, Strategy), not HOW implemented (MobManager, StrategyService)
Responsibilities describe what concept does in business domain (Mob coordinates minions, Strategy determines targets)
Collaborators show which concepts work together (Mob uses Strategy, Strategy identifies Targets)
Relationships reflect business rules (Mob contains Minions, Strategy has TargetCriteria)
Domain language understood by both GMs and developers (avoid pure tech or pure game jargon)
Avoid generic technical terms (Manager, Handler, Service) - use domain nouns (Mob, Strategy, Coordinator)
Favor nouns and resources (Mob, Target, Attack) over verbs (Grouping, Targeting, Attacking)
Domain concepts are technology-agnostic - no JavaScript classes, Foundry API details, or database schema
Start lightweight then add detail - begin with concept names/responsibilities, add relationships/rules as needed
Domain model refinement happens iteratively as understanding deepens through discovery and design phases
Existing Foundry documentation and input.txt are sources for discovery, not the definition of our domain
Sub-epics typically represent bounded contexts - true here (Map Token System, Create Mob, Select Strategy, etc.)
